first_impression.summary_in_own_words: It's a planner page for getting married in Portugal: palaces in Sintra, cliffs in the Algarve, and someone called a Wedded Advisor who plans it with you. But the first thing it tells me is a list of facts about legal paperwork and heat waves, so it reads more like a travel guide than 'here's what we do and what it costs'.

attention_map.quote: Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
attention_map.why: Four separate one-line facts stacked under the headline. Legal process and heat waves before anything about what you'd do for us. The headline 'from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff' is nice though, that made me scroll.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge pairs you with a Wedded Advisor who plans with you from the first ... proposal.
attention_map.why: This is what I actually want, someone to handle it. It's half hidden behind the sticky bar, though.

attention_map.section: Season / guests / Check your date form
attention_map.why: You're asking me how many guests, but you haven't told me what any venue holds. I'm not filling in a form yet.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue (Pena, Monserrate, Queluz, Douro, Algarve cards)
attention_map.quote: The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist: a coloured, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills in a wooded park.
attention_map.why: History lesson. No numbers, no 'fits 80 guests'. And 'Palace roof works run until the first quarter of 2027' on Monserrate made me wonder if it's even available.

attention_map.section: Azulejo tiles and fado guitar images
attention_map.quote: A fado guitar: the Lisbon song UNESCO lists as intangible heritage.
attention_map.why: Pretty filler. Doesn't help me decide anything.
Finally something practical: each region has its airport. Good for working out how our guests get there.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra; nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: Useful to know, honestly, but it's scary. Our wedding could get cancelled for a state event? That's not stress-free.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: a destination wedding in Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: Same palaces, same vineyards, same cliffs again. I'd already seen all this two sections up.

attention_map.section: Pick the Setting for Your Ceremony
attention_map.quote: Some have rooms, so guests can stay where you marry
attention_map.why: The quinta idea with rooms for guests appeals. The rest is a repeat.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill.
attention_map.why: This feels like someone on my side who knows where costs blow out. First time I believed the advisor would actually do something.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Getting There
attention_map.quote: Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide
attention_map.why: Travel times, airports. This is what I'd forward to my partner.

attention_map.section: Entry Rules and Marrying Legally, by Passport
attention_map.quote: The US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI, because no US authority exists to issue one.
attention_map.why: Pages of US and UK passport stuff I scroll past on my phone. The Australian bit is reassuring that it's legal and recognised, but it's a wall of text at 10pm.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: This is the section I scrolled all the way down for and there's not a single number. 'Ask us what drives cost' is a dodge. I still have no idea if 30 to 75k for 60 people is possible.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan.
attention_map.why: I like that it's not a standard package and the list (welcome dinner, long dinner, Sunday brunch, on-the-day coordinator) helps me picture it. But it's 'can include', with no price beside any of it.

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Some quintas have rooms for your closest guests; we check the options nearby for everyone else.
attention_map.why: Half answers where guests stay. 'Start for free' for a guest website is a bit random here.

attention_map.section: Celebrate More Than a Wedding (honeymoon, anniversary, proposal, vow renewal, birthday)
attention_map.quote: Renew your vows on an Algarve cliftop above the Atlantic.
attention_map.why: Not for us right now. More scrolling between me and the bit about who plans it.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor / How It Works
attention_map.quote: Your advisor talks you through your options: regions, venues, the legal route for your passport and what drives cost.
attention_map.why: Clear three steps, and 'every enquiry goes to Wedded Concierge'. But my screenshots end at 'Your Wedded Advisor' so I never see a name or a face.

questions_answered.question: What does this cost all in, and what is included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: No from price anywhere. The costs section says it 'depends on five things' and offers 'Ask us what drives cost'. The weekend list says what it 'can include' with no price.

questions_answered.question: Can it fit our guest count?
questions_answered.evidence: No venue or space capacity anywhere. The form asks 'How many guests?' but nothing tells me what fits. 'Some quintas have rooms for your closest guests' is the closest.

questions_answered.question: Who would actually plan this with us, and what do they do?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Wedded Concierge pairs you with a Wedded Advisor who plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance', the How It Works steps, and the contract checks section. No named person in what I saw; the capture stops at the 'Your Wedded Advisor' heading.

questions_answered.question: How do our guests get there and where do they stay?
questions_answered.evidence: Airports per region (LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC), '15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide', and 'some estates have rooms, so guests can stay where you marry'. Nothing about flights from Australia or where the rest of the guests sleep beyond 'we check the options nearby'.

questions_answered.question: Is our budget realistic for this place?
questions_answered.evidence: No numbers at all, so I can't tell whether Portugal is cheaper or dearer than Italy for us.

objections_triggered.objection: I don't know if my budget is possible for this many people
objections_triggered.triggered_by: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs: 'depends on five things ... We talk you through the options for your plans.'

objections_triggered.objection: Planning from overseas, time zones and suppliers I can't meet
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Long legal and passport sections and the palace conditions ('state events can cancel bookings') make it feel complicated. Partly eased by the advisor and contract checks, but time zones are never mentioned.

objections_triggered.objection: Every planner's page looks the same
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Palaces, vineyards and cliffs repeated in four sections ('Fall for Portugal', 'Choose Your Region', 'See Why Couples Marry', 'Pick the Setting'), with no real weddings.

turn_offs_noticed.where: Whole page, especially 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs'

turn_offs_noticed.turn_off: Generic luxury or heritage adjectives instead of specifics
turn_offs_noticed.where: 'romantic palaces', 'a coloured, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills', 'exotic gardens'
'Which season suits you?' / 'How many guests?' / 'Check your date' right after the hero

emotional_response.felt: Curious about Portugal, a bit overwhelmed by the paperwork, then deflated at the costs section.
emotional_response.stress_free: Not really. The legal and palace-conditions detail made it feel like more work, not less.
emotional_response.authentically_us: The 'no set Portugal package' line and the weekend list got closest.

payload.decision_reason: Portugal looks lovely and the airports, travel times and 'no set package' weekend list are worth sending to my partner, so I'd save it. But I would not enquire: there is no from price, no venue that says it holds our numbers, and no named person in what I saw. My threshold is a price with inclusions, a guest fit and a named planner, and I got none of the three. On the weekend read the costs section would probably still lose us.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, Sintra palaces, that's pretty. Then it's straight into legal process and heat waves. I scroll and scroll, palaces, vineyards, cliffs, then the same palaces and vineyards again. The airports bit is handy, I'll send that to him. The bit about checking contracts so we don't pay for empty rooms, yes, that's exactly what I'm scared of. Then I finally hit 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' and there's no number. Not even a ballpark. 'Ask us what drives cost'. Come on. I don't even know if this is a 40k thing or a 120k thing for 60 people. Saving it, but I'm not filling in a form just to find out if we can afford it.
